drills.q: What decides the clock period for the whole design?
options: The deepest combinational path between any two flip-flops
The average path depth across the design
The slowest single gate in the library
The number of pipeline stages
drills.why: The deadline applies to every path at once and the worst one decides. That is why the number engineers watch is the worst slack across the whole design rather than a typical figure.

drills.q: What are the four things one clock period has to contain?
options: Clock to output, the logic settling, setup time, and clock skew
Fetch, decode, execute, and writeback
Rise time, fall time, propagation delay, and hold time
Setup, hold, metastability window, and jitter
drills.why: Whatever is left over after those four is slack, and getting the worst slack to zero is timing closure, which is most of the schedule of a real chip.

drills.q: What happens when a path misses its setup deadline?
options: The flop captures the old value or a value partway through changing
The result arrives one cycle later than expected
The clock stretches automatically to accommodate it
The design still works but draws more power
drills.why: The intuition from software, that slow means the same answer later, does not transfer. A missed deadline means a wrong value, and the design computes from that wrong value onward.

options: A flop settling to neither 0 nor 1 for an unbounded time before falling one way
A signal oscillating between two values at the clock frequency
A latch that never resolves after reset
Temperature-dependent drift in a gate's switching threshold
drills.why: Its probability is small rather than zero, so a design with a marginal path fails rarely and unpredictably, which survives testing and comes back as a field return nobody can reproduce.

drills.q: What is a hold time violation?
options: A new value races through short logic and reaches the next flop before its input window closes
A value arriving too late for the capturing edge
A clock edge arriving before the previous one has settled
A reset released while the clock is still gated
drills.why: It is the deadline running the other way, and it catches people because it is caused by a path being too fast rather than too slow.

drills.q: Why is a hold violation worse than a setup violation?
options: Slowing the clock fixes setup and does nothing for hold
Hold violations are harder to detect in analysis
Hold violations only appear at high temperature
Setup violations are caught by equivalence checking
drills.why: A chip that fails setup can be sold at a lower speed grade, which is what binning is. A chip that fails hold is scrap, because the race does not care how long the period is.

drills.q: Why do tools insert buffers into paths that are too fast?
options: To add delay on purpose, so a signal arrives after the hold window closes
To strengthen the drive on a long wire
To break up a path that has too much fanout
To equalise the clock arrival at both flops
drills.why: Delay added deliberately, in a design where everything else is a fight to make signals arrive sooner.

drills.q: Why is a ripple carry adder's depth proportional to its width?
options: Each bit's carry feeds the next, so the top bit waits for every stage below
Wider vectors need more buffering to drive
The sum output has more bits to settle
Wider adders use larger and therefore slower cells
drills.why: Doubling the width doubles the delay. It is the canonical chain, and once you have seen it the same shape appears in maxima, selections and accumulators.

drills.q: A maximum of eight values, as a chain and as a tournament. What differs?
options: The arrangement and therefore the depth; the number of comparisons is the same
The tournament uses fewer comparators
The chain gives a different answer on ties
The tournament needs a clock and the chain does not
drills.why: Seven comparisons either way. A chain is seven deep and a tournament is three, and only the second one can be clocked fast.

drills.q: What does a tree cost that a chain does not?
options: Gates, and the area and power that go with them
Latency, because results arrive a cycle later
Correctness on some inputs
Nothing, a tree is better in every respect
drills.why: A chain can reuse one comparator across its steps and a tree needs its own per pair. Trading depth against area is most of what physical design is.

drills.q: What does adding a pipeline stage do?
options: Roughly halves the deepest path and adds a cycle of latency
Halves the path and leaves latency unchanged
Doubles throughput and reduces area
Removes the need for timing analysis on that path
drills.why: Both halves are real. Throughput goes up, which is what you wanted, and any particular result now takes an extra cycle, which somebody pays for.

drills.q: Why is a register at the end of a deep path not a pipeline stage?
options: The path is still as deep as it was; the result just has somewhere to sit
Output registers are optimised away
It inverts the clock polarity of that path
It is, provided the register is wide enough
drills.why: The cut has to be in the middle of the logic. Choosing where is the design work, and it is why the number of stages a unit has is an architecture decision.

drills.q: Why can an accumulator not be pipelined?
options: Its output feeds its own input, so a register inside the loop changes what it computes
Accumulators are always in a different clock domain
The carry chain is not splittable
It can be, but the tools do not support it
drills.why: A register in the loop means adding to a value that is a cycle stale, which is a different function rather than a faster one. The width is the lever that is left.

drills.q: How does static timing analysis know a design's worst path?
options: It walks the netlist with a delay library, considering every path without any input vectors
It simulates with random stimulus and records the slowest observed path
It measures the fabricated chip and back-annotates
It estimates from the total cell count
drills.why: Delay does not depend on the values, only on the structure, which is the same reason the equivalence checker in the last unit needed no vectors either.

drills.q: What is a false path, and why is it a nuisance?
options: A path no input can activate, which analysis still reports and someone has to exclude by hand
A path introduced by the synthesis tool that is not in the source
A path that violates hold but not setup
A path through a clock gate
drills.why: Considering every path is the strength of the method and also its weakness, because "every path" includes the ones that cannot happen.
